tiles.name: diode mixer
tiles.subtitle: ADEX-10L+
tiles.result: about 7 dB of conversion loss from 10 MHz to 1 GHz with +4 dBm of LO (r10 at its top power), IF from DC to 800 MHz, 60 dB L-R isolation
notes: Mini-Circuits ADEX-10L+: two wideband baluns and a ring of four Schottky diodes (drawn beside it on the silk).  The LO
(+4 dBm, +1 to +7) turns the diodes on in pairs, so the RF is multiplied by +-1 at the LO rate: the IF is RF x square
wave, the sum and difference plus odd LO harmonics.  Passive and DC-coupled at IF (a phase detector when RF and LO share
a frequency); 1 dB compression at +1 dBm of RF, IP3 +16 dBm.  Compare r7/r8 (ADL5350) and AMOD-A's a9 (MC1496).

tiles.name: 2.45 GHz filter
tiles.result: 1.7 dB of loss from 2.4 to 2.5 GHz, 30 dB or more below 2.2 GHz and above 2.7 GHz (the datasheet); 50 ohm in and out
notes: Murata LFB212G45SG8A127, a 2012-size LTCC band-pass.  The line to each jack is 50 ohm coplanar waveguide (0.29 mm
wide, 0.25 to the ground pour) with a via fence; the jack's centre pin has no plane under it (a 2.2 mm void).
Sweep it with r10 or r13 into a power meter, or with a DAC harmonic comb and the ADC.

tiles.name: 915 MHz filter
tiles.result: 1.1 dB of loss from 902 to 928 MHz, 40 dB or more 30 MHz outside the band (the datasheet); 50 ohm in and out
notes: RF360 B39921B2672P810: a surface-acoustic-wave filter for the 915 MHz ISM band, 26 MHz wide, in a 1411 package;
its skirts are much steeper than the LTCC's.  Lines, fences and launch voids as on r2.

tiles.name: LNA
tiles.subtitle: QPL9547
tiles.result: 19.5 dB of gain and a 0.3-0.5 dB noise figure from 0.5 to 3 GHz (datasheet: 0.3 dB at 1.9 GHz, OIP3 +39 dBm); 65 mA from 5 V
notes: Qorvo QPL9547: a GaAs pHEMT LNA, internally matched to 50 ohm, 0.1-6 GHz.  It sets the noise figure of every receiver
here, so put it first (before the filter) unless a strong neighbour overloads it; +39 dBm OIP3 makes that rare.
The 18 nH wire-wound choke (Qorvo's value) feeds 5 V into the output pin; 3.3 k from 5 V to Vbias sets 65 mA.
Never cable a transmitter into it without 30 dB of attenuation (22 dBm absolute maximum at the input).

tiles.name: gain block
tiles.subtitle: GALI-84+
tiles.result: 20 dB of gain from 50 MHz to 2.5 GHz (datasheet: 21.9 dB at 1 GHz, 1 dB compression at +20 dBm out); 97 mA from 7.8 V
notes: Mini-Circuits GALI-84+: a Darlington MMIC that sets its own current; the 22 ohm from the 7.8 V rail drops to its
5.8 V device voltage (0.2 W in the 2512).  The 27 nH choke (415 ohm at 2.45 GHz, 155 at 915 MHz) feeds the
output pin; 100 pF blocks keep the DC off the jacks.  Keep the input under 0 dBm for linear gain.  The slide
switch and P-FET gate the tile's 7.8 V as on AMOD-A.

tiles.name: power
tiles.subtitle: USB-C 5 V in: +5, +7.8 V; 25 MHz reference
tiles.result: +5 V from the USB-C (up to 1.5 A), +7.8 V at 250 mA for the gain blocks (yellow LED), a 25 MHz square wave on REF OUT
notes: USB-C power only: 5.1 k on each CC asks any source for 5 V; a 2 A PTC, a 5 V TVS and 20 uF.  The MT3608 boosts to 7.8 V
(0.6 V x 13 from 12 k / 1 k) for the GALI-84+ tile, r12 (100 mA); the +8V rail is a strip under row 1 that their
headers reach with a via.  The TPS7A2033 makes 3.3 V for the TC32H4 TCXO (+-2 ppm) and the 74LVC1G17 that drives
REF OUT (51 ohm: 1.6 Vpp into 50 ohm, 3.3 Vpp into a synthesizer's unterminated REF IN; r10's REF IN passes it to r13).
The TCXO's pad 1 (enable or no connection on the drawing) floats, as CostasLink's review settled.
back: into 50 ohm, to r10 REF IN

tiles.name: TX mixer
tiles.subtitle: ADL5350
tiles.result: RF x LO to IF (or IF x LO to RF) with 7-9 dB of loss from 400 MHz to 2.5 GHz and an IF of 0.1-30 MHz; +4 dBm of LO is enough
notes: ADL5350: a GaAs FET switch mixer with its own LO buffer; the RF and IF pins are one node, split by a crossover
(series 15 pF + shunt 47 nH toward RF, series 47 nH + shunt 15 pF toward IF, corner 200 MHz) in place of the
datasheet's band-tuned tanks: a few dB more loss, every band at once.  The LO's series element is 0 ohm (fit the
datasheet's 3-8 nH for one band); the LO bias choke is 10 nH (the datasheet: 24 nH at 780 MHz, 2 nH at 2 GHz).
Passive, so the same tile up-converts a DAC tone (IF in, RF out) or down-converts an antenna's signal (RF in, IF out).
Both images appear: filter the RF side with r2 or r4.

tiles.subtitle: ADL5350
tiles.result: RF x LO to IF (or IF x LO to RF) with 7-9 dB of loss from 400 MHz to 2.5 GHz and an IF of 0.1-30 MHz; +4 dBm of LO is enough
notes: ADL5350: a GaAs FET switch mixer with its own LO buffer; the RF and IF pins are one node, split by a crossover

tiles.name: synthesizer
tiles.subtitle: MAX2871
tiles.result: any frequency from 23.5 MHz to 6 GHz on OUT A+ and OUT A- (each -4 to +5 dBm in steps, 180 degrees apart), locked to the 25 MHz on REF IN; the red LED says locked
notes: MAX2871 as CostasLink built it: fractional-N PLL with four VCOs, programmed over SPI from the Pmod (SCLK, SDATA,
LE; MUXOUT back).  The loop filter is third order, 80-120 kHz with 61 degrees of margin for both 915 MHz (VCO / 4)
and 2.4 GHz (VCO / 2) at ICP 2.56 mA (RSET 5.1 k, CP = 7).  RFOUTA+ and RFOUTA- each feed a jack through 27 nH to
3.3 V and 100 pF: two outputs, 180 degrees apart; put a 50 ohm terminator on one that is unused.  RFOUTB is open and must
stay disabled.  CE and RFOUT_EN are tied high, LE has 100 k down.  REF IN is unterminated; a back trace takes it on to r13.

tiles.name: I/Q transmitter
tiles.subtitle: TRF3722
tiles.result: I + jQ from two DACs on 0.4-4.2 GHz, about -3 dBm, image-free (-42 dBc untrimmed)
notes: TRF3722 (PLL, VCO, I/Q modulator) on SPI from the Pmod (LE IO6, readback IO5); reference from r10's REF IN.  Each DAC:
56 ohm at the jack, 270 ohm to a node held at 0.25 V (+-0.25 V for +-1 V).  DC on I alone is a CW carrier.
